lines.text: a rumble like a train. Then a wall of molasses.
January 15, 1919. Boston's North End. A giant tank holds two point three million gallons of molasses.
It is suddenly warm after a freezing week, and the tank groans like a ship.
"That tank is leaking!" a worker warns. "Paint it brown," the boss says.
A wave of molasses, twenty-five feet high, charges down the street at thirty-five miles an hour.
"Run!" a man screams. Nobody can run that fast.
It bends the steel of the elevated train tracks and shoves buildings off their foundations.
Picture trying to swim through a pool of glue.
Rescuers wade in. "Over here, I hear someone!" Every step sticks, and the cold makes it thicker.
Twenty-one people die. About one hundred fifty are hurt.
The company blames anarchists. The court blames the company.
After this, building plans need an engineer's signature.
